statement: Let xs be the sequence of values stored in head from front to back, and let n = len(head). Put r = 0 if n = 0, and r = k mod n if n > 0. The function returns a result res. Let ys be the sequence of values stored in res from front to back. Then len(ys) = n, and: (1) if n = 0, ys = [] (so res = Nil); (2) if n > 0, for every i with 0 <= i < n, ys[i] = xs[(i + n - r) mod n]. This is exactly the right rotation of the list by r places, where r is the unique integer in [0,n) congruent to k modulo n.
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result res; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, the number of Cons nodes in res equals the number of Cons nodes in head, i.e. len(res) = len(head).
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: Let xs be the sequence of values in head and ys the sequence of values in res. Whenever the function returns a result res, for every integer v, the number of indices i with ys[i] = v equals the number of indices j with xs[j] = v.
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, every value v occurring in res satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: If rotate_right(head,k1) returns res1 and rotate_right(head,k2) returns res2, then res1 and res2 have the same sequence of node values (equivalently, res1 = res2 as List values).
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; n = len(head) > 0; k1 and k2 are integers with 0 <= k1 <= 2000000000, 0 <= k2 <= 2000000000, and k1 mod n = k2 mod n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, res = head (the same sequence of node values, hence the same List).
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; k = 0.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, res = Nil.
preconditions: head = Nil; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result res, res = head.
preconditions: len(head) = 1; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: Let n = len(head), and let xs and ys be the value sequences of head and res respectively. Put r = 0 if n = 0, and r = k mod n if n > 0. Whenever the function returns a result res: if n = 0 then ys = []; if n > 0 then ys = xs[n-r .. n] ++ xs[0 .. n-r], where xs[a .. b] denotes the contiguous subsequence from index a inclusive to index b exclusive, and ++ denotes concatenation.
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).

statement: Let n = len(head) and r = 0 if n = 0 else k mod n. If the function returns a result res, then for n > 0 the further call rotate_right(res, (n - r) mod n) returns a list whose value sequence equals the value sequence of head (i.e. the rotation is invertible: a right rotation by r followed by a right rotation by n - r restores the original list).
preconditions: len(head) <= 500; every value in head is between -100 and 100 inclusive; 0 <= k <= 2000000000 (k interpreted as an integer).
